mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and generating positive forward returns in the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% over a three-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering investor concerns about weakening corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a broad-based contraction in aggregate demand, increasing the probability of a recession and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 for two consecutive months indicates a weakening in real economic output, signaling reduced corporate profitability and triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO remains below 100 for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the CPIAUCSL above 320.0 with a 12-month growth rate exceeding 3.5% signals persistent inflationary pressure, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain restrictive monetary policy and suppressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 320.0 and 12-month growth exceeds 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both GDP (GDPC1) and residential construction (HOUST) over the past six months indicates strong aggregate demand and housing market momentum, boosting corporate revenues and investor confidence, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint rise in GDPC1 and HOUST fails to predict positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) below 150,000 monthly additions signals labor market weakness, reducing consumer spending power and corporate hiring, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS falls below 150,000 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 combined with a rise in the federal funds rate above 4.0% signals a dual shock of weak supply and tight monetary policy, increasing recession risk and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO < 100 and FEDFUNDS > 4.0%.
